extracted.intended_audience: small business owners, small-entity representatives, and advocates who want to engage in federal rulemaking or report regulatory burdens
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for small businesses and small-entity representatives to engage with federal agencies — via comment letters, roundtables, the Red Tape Hotline, and regional advocates — and to use Advocacy research/resources to influence rulemaking and monitor Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment Letters (Advocacy files)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocacy files comment letters with federal agencies to alert them to their rules’ small business impacts and to propose alternative approaches to achieving regulatory goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When engaging in the notice-and-comment process, emphasize how a proposed rule affects small businesses and, where appropriate, propose less burdensome alternative approaches that still achieve the regulatory objective. See Advocacy's repository of comment letters for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) monitoring and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Regulatory Flexibility Act directs Advocacy to monitor whether proposed federal regulations consider the effects on small businesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should assess and document rule impacts on small entities per the RFA; commenters should frame arguments in terms of RFA considerations (e.g., whether the agency analyzed small-entity impacts and considered alternatives). Use RFA Basics and the RFA Compliance Guide for Agencies to evaluate agency compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Red Tape Hotline reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Through our Red Tape Hotline, business owners can report regulations that may be overly burdensome or costly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the hotline (phone, email, or complaint form) to report specific burdensome regulations. Provide concrete examples and data where possible because tips help guide Advocacy research and inform policymakers. Refer to the Hotline Toolkit for how to submit useful reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roundtables, site visits, and online comments participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Roundtables provide a platform for small business representatives to engage with federal agencies, discuss regulatory issues, and share concerns related to specific industries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participate in Advocacy-hosted roundtables or site visits to share firsthand experiences and industry-specific concerns. Use these venues (and online comment opportunities) to explain regulatory effects, offer practical alternatives, and connect with Advocacy staff who may elevate issues to agencies or Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of economic research and data to support comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocacy produces economic studies, issue briefs, and fact sheets to help policymakers understand what is needed for the start-up, development, and growth of American small businesses and organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground comments and reports to Advocacy in data and economic analysis (e.g., Advocacy's studies, Census-derived data). Citing evidence strengthens claims about regulatory burden and helps shape more persuasive alternatives for agencies and policymakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small business coverage/definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A small business is generally defined as an independent business with fewer than 500 employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When determining whether Advocacy resources or the RFA apply, use this definition (and consult specific SBA size standards if needed). Advocacy supports businesses with fewer than 500 employees, non-profit organizations, and independent contractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact and leverage regional advocates
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocacy has regional advocates in each of the 10 federal regions who interact with small businesses, state and local governments, chambers of commerce, and other communities to support small businesses and learn about potential challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connect with your regional advocate to raise local or industry-specific regulatory roadblocks, request outreach (roundtables/site visits), or get help documenting burdens for comment letters or hotline reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Advocacy guidance resources (guides and toolkits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocacy provides resources such as the Guide to Federal Rulemaking, Small Business Guide to Comment Letter Writing, RFA Basics, RFA Compliance Guide for Agencies, and Hotline Toolkit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before submitting comments or reports, consult these materials for procedural guidance, templates, best practices, and agency-focused compliance information. The 'Small Business Guide to Comment Letter Writing' is the recommended resource for crafting effective comments.
